ClassSummary.description: Units IN THE BAG per class (065). Counts only lines the shop actually supplied — a line marked unavailable is in no bucket. Every field is always present; a client omits a zero when rendering.

packages.description:
Every package the driver was SHOWN at this stop, each with its outcome (063 FR-026: one request, so it cannot half-happen).

⚠ 093 — REQUIRED, AND ONLY WHAT IS NAMED IS SETTLED. Until 093 an absent package meant "collected", so a package added to the stop while the driver stood at the counter was recorded as in the van without anybody having seen it. A package not named here stays waiting, and the stop stays open (`CollectResponse.remaining`).

collected.description: 093 — how many were collected and declared not available by this call.

remaining.description: 093 — packages on the stop this request did not name (added while the driver was there). When more than 0 the stop is still open, and the app re-reads it and shows them.

deliveredBy.description: 082 — who takes it from the hub: an Effy driver, or a courier. What the app says.

items.description: ⚠ THIS PACKAGE'S OWN LINES (065). Until 065 every package at a stop carried every line at the stop, so three packages of 2, 5 and 1 items each read "8 items".

packageCode.description: 089 — the code printed on this package's label (`EFY1:<code>`): bag 1's.

packageId.description: The package's own id — what `CollectRequest.packages[].packageId` names.

parcels.description: 096 — the package's live BAGS, each with its own code ("Bag n of N"). Every step accounts for every bag.

windowLabel.description: 082 — the day and window an Effy parcel is for, in words written by the server; null when none.

CollectionStopDTO.description: GET /driver/v1/collection/runs/{runId}/stops/{stopId} — a shop stop and its packages.

address.description: ⚠ See `CollectionStopSummary.address` — added by 063, retires the `stopAddress` placeholder.

opening.description: 072 — when this stop's round opens; `null` = open. Collecting is refused before then.

address.description:
⚠ ADDED BY 063, AND IT RETIRES A PLACEHOLDER. `collection/data/PlaceholderData.kt` declares `stopAddress = operational("`shop.address`")` — an invented value a driver could act on, so the app renders it as unavailable. 061 built `shop.address_*`; this carries it, and the unblocking condition that placeholder names is now met.

⚠ AN ADDRESS, NEVER A POSITION (D20/D21). The app hands this to the device's own maps app (D7 — per stop, not per route). No coordinate exists to send.

Nullable because a shop whose address has not been recorded yet is an ordinary state the back-office readiness view already reports (061 FR-029/030) — and a driver must be told the address is missing rather than shown an empty line.

parcels.description: 096 — the stop's live BAGS, each with its own code ("Bag n of N"), for matching a scan with no signal.

customerPhone.description: 092 — the phone number the customer gave at checkout, for the driver to call from the door. ⚠ Sent ONLY while the drop is open (not delivered, not failed) and only to the round's own driver; null otherwise, or when the customer gave none. Never in history or run lists.

deliveryWindow.description: 069 — the time window the customer was sold. Null/absent for an order placed before 069. ⚠ Due and late are derived by the app from this and the clock; the server does not send a state that would be stale the moment the screen had been open a minute.

handover.description: 066 — how the customer asked for the order to be handed over, or null/absent for no preference. ⚠ A REQUEST, not a constraint: the app says it and leads the proof chooser with it, and never removes a way of completing the drop. Kept apart from `instructions` because the app ACTS on it.

instructions.description: The customer's NOTE to the driver, verbatim (066). Null when they wrote none. ⚠ Until 066 this was always null: the field existed, three screens rendered it, and nothing stored it. Customer-authored free text — plain text only.

loaded.description: 093 — the van has been loaded with this drop. Until it is, nothing on the drop can be done.

opening.description: 072 — when this drop's round opens; `null` = open. Every action on it is refused before then.

window.description: 069 — the same window as a ready-made label in Melbourne time ("5 pm – 7 pm"), the field the run list has carried since 049. Sent so the app shows the SERVER's wording and never formats a time.

completedAt.description: 092 rev 2 — when a finished drop was finished, and how: the proof method or the failure reason.

deliveryWindow.description: 069 — the same window as instants, so the app can say Due and Late as the clock moves.

parcels.description: 096 — the drop's live BAGS, each with its own code ("Bag n of N"), for matching a scan with no signal.

street.description: 092 rev 2 — the street line, for the run list ("5 Faraday St"); null when the address has none.

summary.description: 065 — the drop's total across its packages, so cold goods show in the list unopened.

window.description: The delivery window as a ready-made label, e.g. "5 pm – 7 pm" (Melbourne time). ⚠ Null from 049 until 069 — the field existed and nothing could fill it, because no window was ever sold.

deadlineAt.description: 072 — the end of the delivery window, or the end of the day where there is none.

opening.description: 072 — when this round opens; `null` = open (always, for a round with no delivery window).

stage.description: 093 — the run's stage and its words.

toReturn.description: 088 — parcels from failed drops on this run, still with the driver, to be checked back in at the hub. `null` when there are none.

DeliveryWindow.description: A same-day delivery window, as two instants.

deadlineAt.description: 072 — the collection run's time: when collecting must be finished.

hubSort.description: 090 — where each package on this run goes at the hub, in the platform's words, so the hub scan can say it with no signal.

stage.description: 093 — the run's stage and its words.

DriverMeDTO.description: GET /driver/v1/me — the record-backed identity read. Display strings only; no currency.

vehicleCheck.description: 093 — today's pre-trip check of the vehicle the driver holds. `due` until it is answered (the driver is given no work until then), `unsafe` until a dispatcher clears it, `none` with no vehicle.

zone.description:
What the driver is cleared to cover, as one line for their own Account screen.

⚠ THE SHAPE IS UNCHANGED BY 062 AND THAT IS DELIBERATE — `apps/driver-mobile` renders it in three places (Today, Help, Account) and it is part of the generated Kotlin contract. What changed is where it COMES FROM: until 062 this was a single assigned zone that no assignment code ever read; it is now DERIVED from the driver's clearances. The app tells the truth without a line of Kotlin changing — the same move 061 made for `DriverVehicle`.

null when the driver is cleared for nothing, which is an ordinary state for a new starter and one the app already renders as unavailable rather than as a broken row.

DriverPhase.description: ⚠ `LocationRequest` STOOD HERE AND IS GONE (061) — see the note below.

DriverRunType.description:
The two kinds of work a driver run can be. Named as a type by 056 because back-office reads it too — it was an inline union used once, and a second consumer is exactly when a concept earns a name (Principle II: one definition per concept, not one per file).

⚠ Work is TYPED TASKS, NOT DRIVER ROLES. One driver typically runs a collection round and then a same-day round in the same shift; neither is a role they hold.

DriverVehicle.description:
What the driver is currently driving, for their own Account screen.

⚠ THE SHAPE IS UNCHANGED BY 061 AND THAT IS DELIBERATE — `apps/driver-mobile` renders it (`DriverMappers.kt`, `AccountScreen.kt`) and it is part of the generated Kotlin contract. What changed is where it COMES FROM: until 061 these were two free-text columns on the driver row that nobody maintained; they are now read from the driver's open `vehicle_holding` and the real vehicle behind it. The app shows a true answer without a single line of Kotlin changing.

Both fields are null when the driver holds no vehicle, which is an ordinary state.

DriverVehicleCheckState.description: 093 — the state of the driver's vehicle check today.

state.description: `due` | `ok` | `unsafe` | `none` — a string on the wire; the app treats an unknown value as `ok`.

vehicleLabel.description: "Toyota HiAce · ABC123", for the check screen's title.

DropPackageRef.description:
One physical package at a drop.

⚠ ONE ENTRY PER PACKAGE SINCE 065, in a stable order the app labels by POSITION ("Package 1 of 2"). A package is one shop's portion, so grouping by package IS grouping by shop — which is why the entry carries no shop id, name or code, and never may.

packageCode.description: 089 — the code printed on this package's label (`EFY1:<code>`): bag 1's.

parcels.description: 096 — the package's live BAGS, each with its own code ("Bag n of N"). Every step accounts for every bag.

to.description: 093 — `out_for_delivery` is written only by loading the van.

acknowledgeHeldPackages.description:
⚠ 064, FR-018 — "I have seen what I am carrying and I am going off duty anyway."

Going off duty with packages still in the van is REFUSED (409) until this is set, and the refusal names every package. It is a confirmation, not a bypass: the requirement is that a shift cannot end SILENTLY on a van with goods in it, not that it cannot end at all — a driver whose van is genuinely empty, or who handed over some other way, says so and goes home.

056 found that standing a driver down could strand physical goods permanently and invisibly: the release sweep deliberately never reclaims picked-up work, so nothing else would ever mention it.

expectedEndAt.description:
⚠ OPTIONAL, AND ITS ABSENCE MEANS UNKNOWN (061, FR-032/FR-033).

When a driver goes on duty they may say when they expect to finish. It buys nothing today — it exists so the dispatch slice can ask "can this driver finish this round before they go home", which is otherwise unanswerable.

⚠ IT MUST NEVER BE DEFAULTED TO A SHIFT LENGTH. An invented finish time would make a guess look like a fact at exactly the moment it decides someone's workload — and the driver would be the one who found out.
null = the driver did not say. Render as "unknown", never as a time.

HandoverMethod.description: 090 — how a package was handed over: scanned from its label, its code typed (a torn label), or ticked by hand. Optional on every hand-over; an app that sends none behaves as before.

HandoverPreference.description:
Delivery instructions — 066-delivery-instructions.

What a customer tells the driver: how to hand the order over, and a short note. The vocabulary, the length limit and the normalisation rule live HERE and nowhere else (Principle II): the two customer surfaces use them to show a remaining-characters count, and the two backends use them to decide. A client holding a looser opinion than the server is how a 300-character note is typed, accepted by the screen and refused at payment.

⚠ THE SERVER IMPORTS THIS FILE. Checkout (`edge-api/commerce`) calls `normaliseDeliveryInstructions` itself, so the client's opinion and the server's are the same function. (Until 070 the server was a second language and carried a mirror, pinned by `delivery-instructions.fixtures.json`; the fixture remains as this rule's table of cases.)

failureReason.description: 092 rev 2 — why a drop came back to the hub.

map.description: 092 rev 2 — a run's map (every stop done), and its window in words.

packageCount.description: 092 rev 2 — a drop's packages, and the window it was sold.

stops.description: 092 — for a RUN: its stops in order, each with how it ended. Absent for a drop. ⚠ Until 092 a run's detail looked its id up as a stop and was always "not found".

failureReason.description: Set for a drop that was NOT delivered (its parcels went back to the hub).

street.description: 092 rev 2 — the street line, how it was handed over, and — for a drop that came back — why.

packageCount.description: 092 rev 2 — packages on the run, and a delivery run's window in words.

HistoryStop.description: 092 — one stop of a finished run, as History lists it. No money, no customer name.

failureReason.description: 092 rev 2 — why a drop came back to the hub.

title.description: The shop's name, the drop's street and suburb, or "Hub check-in".

HubCheckinEffyGroup.description: 082 — the Effy parcels of one check-in that wait for one day and window.

anyTime.description: 085 — these were sold a day with no time.

date.description: yyyy-mm-dd (Melbourne) of the window; null for a parcel sold no window.

dueToday.description: True when these go out TODAY (their window is today, or they were sold no window): the driver loads them for a delivery round. False = shelved at the hub for a later day. ⚠ Decided by the server, which knows the operating day; the app never compares dates.

courierCount.description: 080 — parcels a COURIER takes from the hub. The app says "Courier".

effyCount.description: 082 — parcels EFFY delivers, in all and by the day and window each waits for. The app shows two groups, "Effy delivery" (these) and "Courier", and the driver classifies nothing. ⚠ `label` is written by the server ("Today, 4 pm – 6 pm", "Thu 15 Oct, 10 am – 12 pm"): the app has no timezone database and never formats a day itself. A parcel sold no window has null instants.

held.description: 093 — packages declared not in the van at this check-in, now held for dispatch.

nextCourierPickupLabel.description: 092 — when the courier next collects from the hub, in the server's words ("4 pm", "tomorrow 10 am"); null when no courier parcel was checked in or no courier service is set up.

HubSortInstruction.description: 090 — one package's hub instruction. `label` is the whole line: "LOAD NOW · Today 4–6 pm".

kind.description: `load_now` | `shelve` | `courier_bay` (`HubSortKind`). ⚠ A STRING ON THE WIRE, NOT AN ENUM: the driver app decodes enums as closed sets, and a fourth kind added later would fail the whole run read on every installed build. The app maps an unknown kind to "show the label".

parcelCodes.description: 096 — the codes of every bag of this package: each bag scanned at the hub gets this instruction.

LabelReadDTO.description: One read as the client made and judged it. `clientReadId` makes an offline replay record once; `deviceAt` is when it happened on the device, kept however late it arrives.

LoadRequest.description: POST /driver/v1/delivery/runs/{runId}/load — 090: the van is loaded; every staged drop goes out.

held.description: 093 — packages taken off the run as not loaded, and drops removed because nothing was left.

loaded.description: How many drops this call moved to out for delivery.

LoadStep.description: 093 — "Load the van": the run, and what goes in it.

included.description: False when the shop supplied none of this line. Shown as "not included", never hidden.

qty.description: ⚠ The quantity IN THE BAG (065) — what the shop gathered, which is less than `orderedQty` when the line was part-supplied and 0 when it was not supplied at all. Until 065 this was the quantity ordered, so a driver's count disagreed with the bag whenever a shop was short.

ParcelDTO.description: A live parcel as every surface sees it. `of` = this package's live bags.

ParcelMissingReason.description: Why a bag was not handed over at a step. `other` needs a note.

returned.description: How many parcels this call returned; 0 when nothing was left to return.

roundComplete.description: True when the run is now finished.

ParcelsToReturn.description:
088 — what a driver still has to bring back to the hub from a delivery run's failed drops.

⚠ A FIELD, NEVER A NEW `TodayItemRef.kind`. Installed driver builds decode that kind as a closed enum; a new value would fail the WHOLE Today response on every one of them, and there is no app-update mechanism. An unknown field is ignored by every build.

orders.description: Order numbers only — no address, no customer (049 FR-013).

parcels.description: 092 rev 2 — each parcel, for the Return to hub screen: its ref, where it was for and why it came back.

ParcelsUnaccountedProblem.description: 096 — the 409 a step answers when a live bag was neither handed over nor declared missing.

ProblemFieldIssue.description: RFC 9457 problem+json — the platform's single machine-readable error shape (mirrors docs/api/error-envelope.md from 004). Typed ONCE here (Principle II); every web surface consumes it, never re-declares it.

field.description:
The offending field path — or, for a whole-request refusal, a STABLE MACHINE-READABLE CODE.

⚠ 032 uses the second form for delivery-pricing refusals (`cap_below_floor`, `bands_required`, …). "Please check the fields and try again" tells an operator nothing about which of five rules they broke, and every one of those rules fails SILENTLY in production if it is not understood — a cap below the floor makes every delivery cost the cap, forever.

code.description: A stable, machine-readable refusal code, where the route defines one (069: the checkout's `slot_required` / `slot_unavailable` / `date_unavailable`). A contract value a client switches on and maps to its OWN copy — unlike `detail`, which is prose.

errors.description: ⚠ THE WIRE KEY IS `errors`. `@effy/edge-shared`'s `problem()` has always serialised field issues under `errors`; `fields` was the name only this type used, so every reader keying off it saw nothing. Both are declared so the mismatch is visible here rather than rediscovered per surface (053 found it; 054 fixed the reader in `@effy/api-client`).

parcels.description: 096 — every bag of the drop, handed over or declared missing (`ParcelStepFields`).

ReadMethod.description: How a read was made. A bag ticked by hand is not a read: it is a hand-over with method `manual`.

ReadOutcome.description: What a read means, everywhere (FR-052). `not_found` is decided by the server only.

parcels.description: 096 — the package's live BAGS, each with its own code ("Bag n of N"). Every step accounts for every bag.

RoundOpening.description: 072 — when a round opens. ⚠ ONLY EVER SENT FOR A ROUND THAT HAS NOT OPENED: the server decides "is it open" against its own clock and sends `null` once it is, so a phone whose clock is wrong cannot show an open round as locked.

at.description: The instant, ISO 8601 — what the app's clock is compared with to unlock by itself.

label.description: The same moment in words, Melbourne time. The app never formats a time.

hub.description: The hub's point — also where "Navigate to the hub" goes.

stops.description: In route order: a collection run ends at the hub, a delivery run starts there.

RunMapPoint.description: 092 rev 2 — the RUN MAP (decorative, operator direction 2026-10-17, decision D25): where a run's stops roughly are, so the app can draw a small schematic map. ⚠ A STOP'S POINT IS ITS POSTCODE'S PLACE — the locality the platform already holds — never a geocoded address and never a device position; the hub's is the hub's own. Nothing that orders or assigns work reads it (D20 stands). Stops whose place has no point are left out.

n.description: The stop's number in the run's list; null for the hub.

TemperatureClass.description:
How an item must be carried (065). The driver-facing vocabulary, NOT the catalogue's: the catalogue says `ambient`, a driver is shown "Normal".

⚠ `not_recorded` IS NOT A SYNONYM FOR `normal`. It is a line sold before 065 snapshotted the class, and nobody knows what it was. Showing it as Normal would tell a driver a frozen item can ride in the ambient compartment — the exact harm the class exists to prevent (065 FR-010).

changedNote.description: 092 — what dispatch changed on the current round while it was under way ("Added 2 drops"), in their words; null when nothing has changed. Shown on Today until the driver dismisses it.

deadlineAt.description: 072 — the current round's deadline. `null` only when there is no current round.

dueLabel.description: 072 — the deadline in words, Melbourne time ("2 pm", "tomorrow 11 am").

loadStep.description: 093 — the current run is a delivery run that is open and not loaded: loading is the next step, and `active` is null. Nothing on a drop can be done before it.

opening.description:
072 — when the current round OPENS. `null` means it is open (or there is none).

⚠ WORK IS NOW GIVEN OUT THE MOMENT A DRIVER CAN TAKE IT, hours before it can be done. A round is readable from the moment it is assigned and its actions are refused until it opens — by the platform (a 409 problem of type `round_not_open`, carrying `opensAt` and `opensLabel` as field issues), not merely hidden by the app.

progress.description: 092 rev 2 — progress through the current round, and its map.

stage.description: 093 — the current run's stage (`RunStage`) and the same in words ("Collecting 2 of 5").

toReturn.description: 088 — the current round's parcels still to return to the hub. When that is the only work left on it, `active` is `null` and this is what the driver is shown.

upcoming.description: 072 — the driver's OTHER unfinished rounds, soonest first. Until 072 a driver was told about one round at a time because rounds only existed for the last 45 minutes before they were due.

TodayItemRef.description:
A compact reference to the active/queued work item shown on the home.

⚠ `"hub_checkin"` ADDED BY 064, AND IT FIXES A LIVE DEFECT. A collection round's work did not end at its last shop — the load still has to be checked in at the hub — but the hub had no representation here, so `todayView`'s outstanding filter emptied the moment the final shop stop went `done`. Both routes into the round (the hero card, drawn from `active`, and the "Whole run" link, drawn only when `upNext` is non-empty) vanished at exactly that point. Found live on 2026-09-21 with a driver holding thirteen packages and no way back into their own round.

coldCount.description: Packages holding chilled or frozen goods.

street.description:
092 rev 2 — what the Today card and its "Up next" rows show (the redesign's canvas). All optional: a server without them leaves the card as it was.
- `street`: a drop's street line ("12 Lygon St") — the card's title; null for a shop or the hub.
- `place`: the rest of the place in one line — a shop's full address, or a drop's "Carlton VIC 3053".

window.description: A drop's window, in the server's words, and its instants (for "Due now" / "Late").

TodayProgress.description: 092 rev 2 — how far through the current round the driver is. Counts, never money.

packagesInVan.description: Collection: packages picked up so far / still to pick up.

UpcomingRound.description: 072 — a round the driver holds besides the current one. Readable in full; a count here.

VehicleCheckItem.description: 093 — the six things a driver checks before taking the vehicle out.

WireInt.description:
A whole number on the wire.

⚠ THIS ALIAS IS LOAD-BEARING, and it exists because a plain `number` broke every mobile cart write.

TypeScript `number` becomes JSON Schema `"number"`, which the Kotlin generator renders as `Double` — so `kotlinx.serialization` sent `"quantity":1.0`, and Go's `encoding/json` **cannot** unmarshal `1.0` into an `int`. Every `POST /v1/cart/items` and `PATCH /v1/cart/items/{id}` from customer-mobile therefore failed to bind and answered 422. `customer-web` was unaffected: JavaScript serialises an integer as `1`, with no decimal point.

`@asType integer` makes the schema say `"integer"`, which generates a Kotlin `Long` and puts a whole number on the wire. Use it for EVERY count, quantity, limit and revision in this contract — the response direction was always fine (kotlinx accepts `3` for a Double), so the asymmetry hid it.

See specs/027-customer-cart-sync/research.md R13.
